canon_statuses.ALTERNATE_CONTINUITY: True only inside a separate continuity (e.g. Echoverse).
canon_statuses.CANON_CONFIRMED: Stated by a cited Wizards primary source.
canon_statuses.CANON_DISPUTED: Sources or in-story narrators conflict; both accounts are preserved.
canon_statuses.CANON_IMPLIED: Strongly implied by a cited primary source but not stated outright.
canon_statuses.HYPOTHETICAL: Creative or deckbuilding connection; never canon.
canon_statuses.OPEN_QUESTION: Primary sources leave the matter unresolved; do not assert either way.

nodes.name: The Sylex (as named in Return to Dominaria Ep. 9)
Ajani, Nacatl Pariah // Ajani, Nacatl Avenger
Nicol Bolas, the Ravager // Nicol Bolas, the Arisen

nodes.limitation: This does not establish the entire genealogy of all later dragons.
nodes.name: Ugin and Nicol emerge together as twin dragons in the story's account of the original dragons' hatching.

nodes.limitation: Interpret the twins' motives from the described actions; a single psychological explanation is not a canon rule.
nodes.name: Their early responses to threats and mortal civilizations show contrasting priorities, which the Chronicle develops into their later conflict.

nodes.limitation: This is Bolas's self-serving narrated list, not an independently certified exhaustive Elder Dragon War casualty roll.
nodes.name: Bolas describes these four Elder Dragons as surviving when he later returned to Dominaria.

nodes.limitation: His claim to be the first or alone is a narrator claim, not objective proof of priority over every planeswalker.
nodes.name: Bolas reports his first planeswalk and discovery of the connected Multiverse.

nodes.limitation: Do not collapse the original timeline into the subsequent changed Tarkir history.
nodes.name: The rivals fight over ancient Tarkir in the historical confrontation that Sarkhan later alters.

nodes.limitation: This action changes Tarkir's history; it does not simply occur after the original death in one unchanged sequence.
nodes.name: Sarkhan travels into Tarkir's past and prevents Ugin's death; the dragon tempests and later draconic dominance persist.

nodes.limitation: Distinguish this Meditation Realm confrontation from the separate Sarkhan-modified Tarkir death event.
nodes.name: The Chronicle portrays Bolas seemingly killing Ugin in the Meditation Realm and Ugin persisting as a spirit-like presence.

nodes.limitation: This was the situation in 2019, not Bolas's status after later Tarkir: Dragonstorm.
nodes.name: Following War of the Spark, Bolas loses his spark and is held in the Meditation Realm under Ugin's guard.

nodes.limitation: An escape is not evidence that he recovered his planeswalker spark or arrived at a particular destination.
nodes.name: The Meditation Realm prison fails during Tarkir: Dragonstorm, freeing Bolas; the later Lorwyn story confirms he escaped.

nodes.limitation: Do not infer all subsequent activities or power changes from this one scene.
nodes.name: Ugin returns visibly to Tarkir and tells others that he failed to keep Bolas imprisoned.

nodes.limitation: Do not invent restored planeswalking ability or assert a confirmed permanent spark loss after the escape.
nodes.name: The later story explicitly leaves open whether Bolas still has his spark after his escape.

nodes.limitation: This alternate-reality statement must never erase or override Bolas's presence in the prime Multiverse.
nodes.name: The Reality Fracture guide describes Jace's Echoverse as a different history without Bolas.

nodes.limitation: The sequence is not an exhaustive census of their elder kin.
nodes.name: The Chronicle portrays the young twins meeting Arcades, Chromium and Palladia-Mors during their early travels.

nodes.limitation: The lineage claim is voiced by the raiders within a framed story, not a genealogy of each attacker.
nodes.name: The embedded tale identifies the raiders of Bolas's kingdom as Vaevictis's descendants, according to the raiders themselves.

nodes.limitation: Specific provocations in a reconstructed tale do not establish every cause of a long, continent-spanning war.
nodes.name: The Chronicle shows Nicol exploiting conflict around Vaevictis and deliberately inciting other dragon branches, including Palladia-Mors.

nodes.limitation: Narrative participation alone does not make Arcades a loyal ally of Ugin or Bolas.
nodes.name: The Chronicle's war account specifically includes Arcades leading followers into conflict with dragon kin.

nodes.limitation: Bolas did not personally fight every dragon or control every faction in the conflict.
nodes.name: Wizards' later editorial history explicitly credits Nicol Bolas with instigating the Elder Dragon War.

nodes.limitation: Bolas's narrated roster is incomplete; this is not proof of the total number of all survivors or an automatic retcon.
nodes.name: Wizards' Piru biography names Piru and Chromium among the Elder Dragon War survivors; Piru is absent from Bolas's four-name account.

nodes.limitation: The editorial biography does not establish Crosis as their direct first-generation offspring.
nodes.name: Piru and Chromium were mates and their descendants include Primeval Dragon Crosis, the Purger.

nodes.limitation: This later battle is not part of the Elder Dragon War itself.
nodes.name: Millennia after the war, Geyadrone Dihada bound Piru and Chromium to fight Dakkon Blackblade.

nodes.limitation: Their fates must not be added to the Elder Dragon War casualty list.
nodes.name: Dakkon slew Piru and banished Chromium in the later conflict engineered by Dihada.

nodes.limitation: The biography does not give a precise in-universe date.
nodes.name: Piru's death caused a magical blast that cracked Dominaria's crust at the Dueling Chasm of Corondor.

nodes.limitation: This parentage does not imply Rith participated in the much earlier Elder Dragon War.
nodes.name: Wizards' Dominaria United biography directly identifies Rith as Palladia-Mors's daughter.

nodes.limitation: The source does not fix exact reign dates or identify every Primeval's parent.
nodes.name: Rith was among five ancient Primeval Dragons who ruled Dominaria sometime after the Elder Dragon War.

nodes.continuity: time travel to shared Tarkir past
nodes.limitation: This relative interval is the 2015 story's account, not an absolute Multiverse calendar date.
nodes.name: Sarkhan crosses into Tarkir's past, approximately 1,280 years before his original present, to change a decisive ancient battle.

nodes.limitation: Neither the artwork nor the story alone assigns every individual magical strike to a unique printed card.
nodes.name: Nicol Bolas confronts Ugin in Tarkir's skies while Sarkhan observes the encounter.

nodes.limitation: This describes the scene, not proof that a specific Yasova card illustration depicts the spell.
nodes.name: Yasova's rune-guided spell enables Bolas's ambush and redirects dragons called by Ugin to attack Ugin instead.

nodes.continuity: revised Tarkir timeline created by intervention
nodes.limitation: The revised history must remain separate from the original branch where dragons later disappeared.
nodes.name: Sarkhan creates a protective hedron cocoon around the gravely wounded Ugin, changing what would have been Ugin's death.

nodes.limitation: Design intent does not guarantee the Nexus artwork depicts Sarkhan actually using the gateway.
nodes.name: Wizards' card-design account explicitly identifies Ugin's Nexus as the time-travel mechanism built for Sarkhan's story.

nodes.limitation: This proves Wizards used that named card art in the scene; it does not match every reprint art variant or every frame of the duel.
nodes.name: The official illustrated story captions Crux of Fate (art by Michael Komarck) immediately at the scene where Ugin and Nicol face each other.

nodes.limitation: A location art caption is not proof that its illustration shows the 1,280-year-earlier combat itself.
nodes.name: The Chronicle captions Crucible of the Spirit Dragon art beside the characters' description of Ugin's canyon and protective hedron cocoon.

nodes.limitation: The site was interpreted as a tomb by characters; Ugin's later survival changes the interpretation of the same place.
nodes.name: Official Tarkir stories use Tomb of the Spirit Dragon card art in accounts of searching for and returning to Ugin's burial site.

nodes.limitation: Birth order and childhood (Tocasia, Koilos) are not covered by the sources fetched for this pack.
nodes.name: Urza and Mishra are brothers; Tawnos tells Kayla that Urza's brother was turned and fused with a machine.
Kayla bin-Kroog, princess of Kroog, is Urza's wife and rules Penregon after the war.

nodes.limitation: His death is reported through Kayla's dialogue; its circumstances are not narrated here.
nodes.name: Harbin is Kayla's son by Urza; he served as a pilot and officer and did not return from the war.
Tawnos is Urza's former assistant and an artificer who returns to Penregon in 69 AR.

nodes.limitation: Kayla also calls Ashnod Mishra's torturer of Tawnos and, by rumor, his lover; the rumor is not graded as fact.
nodes.name: Ashnod was an artificer who worked for Mishra during the war; Tawnos names transmogrants as her work.

nodes.limitation: The design article and dialogue do not narrate the full mechanism of corruption.
nodes.name: Mishra was corrupted by the Phyrexians (cards: Mishra, Claimed by Gix; Mishra, Lost to Phyrexia); Tawnos says he was turned by 'that creature' and fused with a machine.
Urza activated the Golgothian Sylex on Argoth and ended the war.
The Last Battle took place on Argoth, an island shattered and buried by the sylex blast; by 69 AR it is reduced to basalt spires.
Teferi witnesses a spark coalescing where Urza's body burned away inside the detonation; Urza becomes a Planeswalker.

nodes.limitation: Stated in an official design article describing card art and story.
nodes.name: When Urza became a Planeswalker, the Mightstone and Weakstone became his eyes.

nodes.limitation: Sequence only; the physical causal chain is not explained in the fetched text.
nodes.name: Episode 5 places the Shard of Twelve Worlds and the Ice Age after the detonation, and ends with the Ice Age upon Dominaria.

nodes.limitation: Official text frames these as competing legends; no single origin is canon in this source.
nodes.name: Episode 5 deliberately gives incompatible origins for the sylex: found or made by Feldon, carved by Ashnod, pulled from Old Phyrexia by Gix, a giant's tooth, Tal's tear, and more.
Urza's obsession with Dominaria's history led to a millennia-long vendetta against Yawgmoth and Phyrexia.

nodes.limitation: Yawgmoth's own Thran-era origin is not stated in the fetched official sources.
nodes.name: As a young man Urza was obsessed with the history of Dominaria and the Thran Empire that once ruled the plane.

nodes.limitation: The profile does not name the event; novel-era detail (Invasion/Apocalypse) is not ingested.
nodes.name: After countless years of conflict, Urza and Yawgmoth perished together.
Teferi's spirit is sent back in time to witness how the sylex works firsthand.
Karn unearths the Golgothian Sylex; Ajani, revealed as a Phyrexian sleeper agent, destroys it.
Saheeli crafts a replica of the sylex whose workings are unknown.

nodes.limitation: Profile-level summary; the Weatherlight Saga novels/comics (Weatherlight through Apocalypse) are not ingested.
nodes.name: The skyship Weatherlight, its crew of heroes, and the Legacy were instrumental in thwarting Phyrexia's invasion of Dominaria.

nodes.limitation: Other Legacy components are not enumerated by the cited source.
nodes.name: The Legacy was a collection of artifacts that included the Planeswalker Karn.

nodes.limitation: Origin of that technology (Thran) is not stated in the cited source.
nodes.name: The Weatherlight contained ancient magical technology that enabled the ship to planeswalk.

nodes.limitation: Absolute date and construction details not given.
nodes.name: Karn is a sentient silver golem created over 1200 years ago (relative to the profile) by the Planeswalker Urza.
Karn created Mirrodin, an independent metallic plane with five colored suns.
Old Phyrexia was destroyed but Karn became an unwitting carrier of its oil, and accidentally left a drop of glistening oil on Mirrodin's inner core.

nodes.limitation: Scars of Mirrodin story chronology is summarized, not ingested episode by episode.
nodes.name: The oil slowly corrupted Mirrodin from the inside out; Mirrans became Phyrexians and the plane became New Phyrexia.

nodes.limitation: The Thran-era origin story (novel The Thran) is not ingested; 'medical genius' is the only biographical detail used.
nodes.name: Yawgmoth was a medical genius from Dominaria.
Yawgmoth planeswalked to Old Phyrexia and installed himself as its new ruler, the Father of Machines.

nodes.limitation: Do not name a creator from non-Wizards sources.
nodes.name: Old Phyrexia was an artificial plane created by an unknown Planeswalker; the creator is not identified.
Yawgmoth used the Phyrexians to launch repeated invasions of his home plane.

nodes.limitation: Accounts may be complementary rather than contradictory (shared final battle); the Apocalypse novel is not ingested, so the precise sequence is unresolved here.
nodes.name: Official summaries credit Yawgmoth's end differently: the ONE guide says he was slain by Karn and his allies; the 2022 Dominaria guide credits Gerrard with bringing about his defeat; the Urza profile (Pack B) says Urza and Yawgmoth perished together. All accounts are preserved.

nodes.limitation: The guide states Old Phyrexia was destroyed but does not explicitly tie the destruction to the same battle.
nodes.name: Old Phyrexia was destroyed after Yawgmoth's defeat.
During the first Phyrexian Invasion, Dominaria's inhabitants formed the Coalition, an alliance spanning many species, peoples and nations.

nodes.limitation: The 2018 Return to Dominaria rebuild arc is not claim-extracted episode by episode.
nodes.name: After rebuilding the skyship, Jhoira handed the captaincy to Shanna and retired to her workshop at the Mana Rig.
Shanna took over as captain of the Weatherlight when Jhoira gave up control.

nodes.limitation: Applies to the DMU-era Coalition.
nodes.name: When news of the Phyrexian invasion reached her, Jhoira joined the Coalition and serves as one of its leaders.
Jodah, an archmage over 4,000 years old, uses his reputation to rally allies to the Coalition's banner.

nodes.limitation: The source does not name the war or the ancestor.
nodes.name: Jodah was born when 'his ancestor's war' had decimated Terisiare, implying the Brothers' War.
Praetor Sheoldred leads a new invasion of Dominaria.
Raff Capashen is navigator and ship's mage for the Weatherlight.
House Capashen's heritage stretches from ancient Sheoltun nobility to the hero Gerrard.

nodes.limitation: Fills part of the Pack B Koilos gap; the powerstone split (Mightstone/Weakstone) is still not sourced.
nodes.name: Urza and Mishra discovered ancient stones of power in the Caves of Koilos.
The stones of power were found in the Caves of Koilos.
At the end of the Brothers' War, Urza discovered the plane of Phyrexia.

nodes.limitation: Participants in the Mending are not named in the cited source.
nodes.name: Dominaria was the epicenter of temporal-planar fractures; a handful of powerful Planeswalkers mended the rifts.

nodes.limitation: Homeland not named in the profile (do not assert Zhalfir from this source).
nodes.name: Teferi phased his homeland out of time, later lost his spark, and new threats inspired him to reclaim it.
The Machine Orthodoxy, under Elesh Norn, sought a leader to replicate the glory days of Yawgmoth; Norn later embraced the role of Mother of Machines.
Jhoira raises the sunken Weatherlight with merfolk and a human salvage crew and begins rebuilding it.
After Amonkhet, Nissa leaves the Gatewatch and Dominaria.
Belzenlok is the last demon of Liliana's pact; Gideon stays on Dominaria to help her kill him.

nodes.limitation: Narrated from Liliana's point of view.
nodes.name: Belzenlok supplanted the god Kuberr to take control of the Cabal.
Belzenlok is worshipped by the Cabal, a death cult, from its Stronghold in Urborg.

nodes.limitation: Belzenlok's claims are in-story propaganda; this pack does not resolve the forger.
nodes.name: Cultists credit Belzenlok with forging the Blackblade and slaying an elder dragon; a disciple starts to name Dakkon Blackblade instead, and Jhoira says Belzenlok takes credit for every shift in Dominaria's history.
Long ago, Liliana's attempt to heal her brother Josu turned him undead.
Liliana's spark ignited as she fled Dominaria after Josu's transformation.

nodes.limitation: The Raven Man's identity is not established in this pack.
nodes.name: The Raven Man manipulated Liliana into the healing work that undid Josu.
Belzenlok made Josu his lich and general in Caligo.
At Vess Manor, Liliana uses the Chain Veil to unmake the lich Josu and end the curse of House Vess.
Shanna is a descendant of Captain Sisay and carries her sword; she joins the Weatherlight crew.
Danitha Capashen is distantly related to Gerrard; she declines Jhoira's invitation.
Urza created the Weatherlight's Powerstone by collapsing Serra's Realm into it.
Tiana's prayer revives the inert Powerstone.
Tiana, an angel of Serra, realizes she is the Weatherlight's guardian angel.
Arvad is a Knight of Benalia who was captured and made a vampire.

nodes.limitation: 'White star' is Slimefoot's perception; identifying it with the Powerstone is an inference.
nodes.name: Arvad was drawn across the world to the ship by what Slimefoot perceives as the 'white star'.
The saproling Slimefoot sprouted and grew aboard the Weatherlight.
Venser gave his spark to Karn to rescue him and died.

nodes.limitation: These are in-story assessments; later official stories show a Phyrexian threat to Dominaria.
nodes.name: Ajani tells Jhoira the Phyrexians are contained on one fallen plane; Jaya doubts the common belief that they are no longer a threat.
Jhoira says the Blackblade killed an elder dragon; Shanna names Piru, hedged with 'I think'.
The Blackblade is a soul-drinker that steals the life-energy of everything it kills.
During the Phyrexian Invasion, Teferi phased Zhalfir partially out of Dominaria to spare it.
Teferi spent his spark repairing Shiv's time rift, which left him unable to return Zhalfir.
Niambi made a Powerstone at the Thran Mana Rig that holds Teferi's spark.

nodes.limitation: Ep. 11 states he took it back; that the stone in Ep. 6 is the mechanism is an inference across episodes.
nodes.name: Teferi takes his spark back to join the fight against Bolas.
Luti, the old woman at the Keral Keep monastery, was Jaya Ballard in disguise.
Chandra seeks Jaya Ballard on Dominaria to learn from her.
Karn excavates the Sylex and intends to detonate it on New Phyrexia.

nodes.limitation: The episode says 'the Sylex'; identity with the Golgothian Sylex is inferred.
nodes.name: The Sylex harmed Multani in the past, which implies the Golgothian Sylex of Argoth.

nodes.limitation: In-story statement by Karn; see Pack B B012.
nodes.name: Karn says Urza created the Sylex; Pack B (B012) preserves competing official origin legends.
A semiconscious Multani attacks the dig site, fearing the Sylex.
The Cabal Stronghold was first built as a Phyrexian base.
Gideon carries the Blackblade into the fight, and Liliana uses it to drain and kill Belzenlok.
The crew recovers the Blackblade from the Stronghold's fourth treasury vault before the final battle.
After Belzenlok dies, Bolas reveals that Liliana's pact now binds her to him.
Radha is freed from the Cabal's prison after the Stronghold falls.

nodes.limitation: Stone and Blood dates this to six thousand years before Eldritch Moon; this pack records no AR year.
nodes.name: Ugin, Sorin and Nahiri together imprisoned the Eldrazi titans on Zendikar.
Nahiri and Sorin named the chamber at the centre of the prison the Eye of Ugin.
Nahiri stayed on Zendikar as the Eldrazi prison's warden.
Ugin and Sorin agreed to come back if the prison needed them.

nodes.limitation: The reasons for Ugin's absence are not stated in this source.
nodes.name: When the Eldrazi nearly escaped, neither Ugin nor Sorin answered, leaving Nahiri to contain them alone.
After the Eldrazi escaped, Sorin came to Tarkir looking for Ugin.

nodes.limitation: The quote does not say who or what freed Ugin, so this claim does not credit Sorin.
nodes.name: In the rewritten timeline, Sorin finds Ugin alive and newly freed; in the original timeline he had found Ugin long dead.
Sarkhan's intervention in the past left Ugin alive but dormant (see A006/A028).

nodes.limitation: The conversation itself is not shown in this source.
nodes.name: In the new timeline, the planeswalker Narset sets out to speak with Ugin, and Sarkhan counts all three as planeswalkers.
Jace travels to the Eye of Ugin to learn about the hedron network.
Ugin told Jace not to kill the titans and not to let them escape.
Sorin and Nahiri were absent when the titans fell, so Ugin's alliance did not reunite.
In Tarkir: Dragonstorm, Jace seizes the gem between Ugin's horns and draws on its power to command the Meditation Realm.
As Bolas broke free, Ugin threw himself at his brother and failed to hold him (see A009).

nodes.limitation: This is Narset's point of view; 'dead now, perhaps' is her uncertainty, which the text itself then resolves.
nodes.name: Narset sees Ugin and Bolas vanish; the same episode states both survived (consistent with A009/A010).

nodes.limitation: The text names Elspeth's voice; that the 'mailed hands' are hers is inferred, not stated.
nodes.name: Elspeth calls to Narset, and armoured hands carry Narset into the Omenpath.
